newsitem.title: DENMARK: Denmark says rail shakeup not part of selloff plan.
newsitem.headline: Denmark says rail shakeup not part of selloff plan.

text.p: Danish Transport Minister Jan Troejborg said on Thursday that plans to re-organise state-run DSB railways into separate companies would not entail a sale of the government's holdings.
"There are no plans to sell shares in the two companies," he told a news conference, adding that restructuring the heavily loss-making railway was likely to take at least until 1998.
"It's a very complicated piece of work," he said.
Control of infrastructure would pass to a new track authority which would lease access to the two DSB urban and intercity companies and to private competitors as they emerged.
Industry sources expect that the government will eventually offer shares in the new companies to the public if it can succeed in making them attractive.
Troejborg hinted as much when he said that in reducing its ownership of other concerns the government's principle had been "to sell where there are buyers."

The market is constantly speculating as to when the government will sell its remaining 51 percent in telecoms giant Tele Danmark and there is talk that the sale of shares in DSB's already-restructured shipping arm is on the agenda in budget negotiations in progress between the government and opposition. --Soeren Linding Jakobsen, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33 969653
